thread:
alex: Hey team — seeing a burst of 502s and huge P95 on /v1/generate starting ~17:41 UTC. Dashboard shows most traffic landing in eu-west1 even though the project is locked to us-west2. This started when we switched to batching 20 requests per RPC. Anyone else got this? :eyes:
jess: Can you paste your failover policy and the request example you used for batching? Sounds like routing/aggregation might be treating the batch differently.
alex: Failover policy attached (redacted):
```json
{
  "mode": "failover",
  "regions": ["us-west2", "eu-west1"],
  "sticky": true,
  "sticky_ttl": "30m",
  "weights": {"us-west2": 0.7, "eu-west1": 0.3}
}
```
Our client bundles 20 independent user requests into one RPC with no session header. Example curl that reproduces: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/batch_generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"requests":[{"prompt":"a"},...], "batch_id":"b-123"}'
```
maria: Quick questions: are you using the batch endpoint or client-side multiplex? Also did you observe any capacity alerts from eu region?
alex: Using server batch endpoint. No capacity alerts for us-west2; surprisingly eu shows higher capacity available during spike. 502s correspond to requests routed to eu, then auth failures for some keys (weird).
kyle: I pulled traces for thread b-123: routing step shows aggregator deciding region per-batch, not per-subrequest. Because the batch had no session cookie, sticky routing was skipped and the routing decision used a "capacity-first" policy introduced in the last rollout for batched RPCs. That picks highest available capacity region. EU returned faster for the short warmup window so the whole batch went there.
alex: Ah — so the change treats a batch as an atomic unit and can override explicit project pinning? We definitely pinned this project to us-west2 in the console.
jess: It shouldn't override project-level pinning. Looking at the policy compiler logs, a bug in the batch-routing codepath was reading the "regions" list backwards when a weight object was present and then falling back to capacity heuristics if pins didn't match compiled constraints. I have a snippet from infra-bot: 
```
[infra-bot] policy-compile(batcher): regions_order=[eu-west1, us-west2] // unexpected
[infra-bot] batch_router: sticky_header_missing=true -> capacity_mode
```
oncall: Filing immediate hotfix: reverting the batch-routing rollout flag for all zones. Can you reproduce after revert?
alex: After revert (17:56 UTC) our hit rate to us-west2 returned to normal and 502s dropped to baseline. Thanks. Repro steps I used: 1) enable batching=20 on client 2) send 60 concurrent batch RPCs 3) observe region in trace (span: routing.region) 4) check HTTP response and auth errors for any cross-region hits.
maria: Root cause summary for ticket: batch-routing rollout had a bug in the compiler that reordered regions when weights were present, and the batch path switched to capacity-first when sticky headers were absent. For batched RPCs without per-user session headers, this caused whole batches to go to a different region despite project pinning.
jess: Action items: 1) revert rollout (done) 2) fix compiler ordering edge-case 3) add automatic test to simulate batched RPC + weights + pinning 4) add instrumentation to flag batch->region switches when project pin is explicit.
akex: small note (for docs): call out that batching can change routing semantics unless session pinning is provided. We'll add client guidance to set X-Redwood-Session or per-subrequest session ids for mixed-user batches.
kyle: Filed infra ticket INF-2026 with repro and logs. Will target patch and staged rollout next week.
alex: thanks all, attaching a short trace + sample payload to the ticket. :thumbsup:
